statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail remains below the blocking threshold because fresh post-reopen NQ one-way structure is not independently verified despite extreme oil and rates stress.
recommendation: Current public policy mapping is WATCH; Stress remains extreme, while any Tail escalation remains contingent on verified persistent directional efficiency and failed mean reversion.
headline: Extreme macro stress persists while post-reopen Tail remains below the block threshold
body: U.S. equities closed lower, Brent settled at $107.63 and the 10-year Treasury yield reached about 4.95%. Oracle rose about 7% after hours, adding a conflicting technology catalyst. Fresh exact NQ post-reopen structure is unavailable, so Tail remains WATCH ahead of CPI.

lookbackSummary: Over the prior 24 clock-hours, Tail moved from low/watch overnight to elevated after the PPI and U.S. cash-open sequence, then returned to WATCH as persistent one-way mean-reversion failure was not sustained or freshly verified.
outlookSummary: Overnight Tail can ease if futures remain two-sided, but oil, yields and geopolitical risk keep Stress extreme. CPI at 12:30 UTC, the 13:30 UTC cash open and Michigan data at 14:00 UTC are the next major checkpoints; Tail escalation requires observed persistence, failed retracements or session-extreme holding.

forecast.analysis: Cash markets closed lower while Oracle rose about 7% after hours, Brent settled above $107 and the 10-year yield reached about 4.95%. Fresh post-reopen NQ path evidence is not independently verified, so Tail stays WATCH.

forecast.analysis: Overnight Tail can ease only if futures remain two-sided after the Oracle/Adobe earnings reaction; renewed one-way extension would invalidate that easing while oil and rates keep Stress extreme.
With U.S. cash closed, thinner liquidity increases headline sensitivity. Orderly retracements and stable energy/rates would support lower WATCH; a fresh geopolitical gap would reverse that path.
Late-U.S./early-Asia trade is expected to stay event-sensitive. Tail remains conditional on whether any directional move permits meaningful retracement rather than simply on the size of the move.
drivers: Directional efficiency is the escalation test

forecast.analysis: During the quieter overnight window, a stable futures range would lower Tail pressure. Persistent extension aligned with oil or yields would be the main reason for a higher path.
Pre-Asia handoff risk is lower if no new shipping or energy disruption emerges. Extreme Stress persists because crude and long yields remain elevated ahead of CPI.
drivers: CPI remains the next major checkpoint

forecast.analysis: Asia participation may add liquidity without changing the baseline if NQ remains two-sided. A one-way regional move with shallow pullbacks would be a Tail escalation checkpoint.
Asia trading remains a confirmation window: stable megacap/semiconductor tone would support easing, while renewed tech weakness plus higher yields would challenge it.
Approaching Europe, overnight range quality matters more than event importance. Tail rises only if price structure becomes directionally efficient and resistant to retracement.
European participation may amplify cross-asset moves. A balanced response to oil and rates supports WATCH; repeated extension across futures and semis would raise the conditional Tail path.
Mid-European trade becomes more CPI-sensitive. Stress stays extreme, but Tail remains below the block threshold unless directional efficiency is already visible before the U.S. data window.
Pre-U.S. positioning can become choppy as CPI approaches. Gap formation without sustained follow-through would remain Stress; repeated failed retracements would be the stronger Tail signal.
The hour before CPI carries high event risk but no release outcome is assumed. Tail remains WATCH unless an already-observed pre-release trend is one-way and reinforced by oil, yields and tech.
August CPI is scheduled for 12:30 UTC. The forecast treats the print as a checkpoint: only observed post-release persistence, shallow pullbacks or failed retracements would justify Tail escalation.
drivers: No hypothetical result treated as fact

forecast.analysis: The U.S. cash open occurs within this hour after CPI. Tail stays WATCH conditionally; opening-auction continuation near extremes with weak retracements would be the key escalation pattern.
Michigan sentiment and inflation expectations are scheduled for 14:00 UTC. A second information wave matters only if it reinforces an already persistent post-CPI price path.
drivers: Second-wave reaction only matters if persistence is observed

forecast.analysis: After the main U.S. data sequence, orderly retracement and volatility decay would support easing within WATCH. Persistent extension through the morning would delay that normalization.
Midday U.S. trade should allow Tail to ease if cross-assets stabilize and NQ mean reversion functions normally. Continued oil/yield pressure alone primarily sustains Stress.
drivers: Oil/yields sustain Stress more than Tail

forecast.analysis: Early afternoon becomes a test of whether any post-CPI trend is durable. Two-sided rotation lowers Tail; renewed extension after failed pullbacks would raise it.
drivers: Failed pullbacks would be the escalation test

forecast.analysis: Later U.S. trade can normalize if volatility and breadth stop reinforcing a directional move. Geopolitical headlines remain an external discontinuity risk.
Power-hour conditions are still conditional: session-extreme holding with shallow pullbacks would be a stronger Tail signal than the day's headline volatility by itself.
Into the cash close, absence of repeated extension supports a low-WATCH path. A late second leg aligned with yields, oil and technology would invalidate that easing.
Post-close risk falls if the day ends with meaningful retracement and cross-asset stabilization. Unresolved geopolitical escalation can keep Stress elevated even with low Tail.
The final forecast hour assumes no new discontinuity and functioning mean reversion. Tail would remain low only if the prior U.S. session failed to develop persistent one-way structure.
drivers: Functioning mean reversion is the baseline

forecastDetail.comment: Observed cash-close weakness, Oracle's after-hours gain, extreme oil/rates stress and unavailable fresh NQ path evidence keep the current mapping at WATCH.
Two-sided post-earnings trade would support easing; renewed one-way extension would invalidate it while macro Stress stays extreme.
Thinner liquidity increases headline sensitivity, but Tail depends on retracement failure rather than move size alone.
Asia handoff conditions are expected to stay event-sensitive; sustained directional efficiency is the escalation checkpoint.
A stable overnight range lowers Tail pressure; persistent extension aligned with oil or yields would reverse that path.
Pre-Asia headline risk remains elevated, while the next major scheduled checkpoint is CPI.
